label: PF Backlog 643
title: Guard: commit branch must match the item id in the message

brief.problem: Guard: commit branch must match the item id in the message
brief.what_adds: Guard: commit branch must match the item id in the message
brief.why: Guard: commit branch must match the item id in the message

objective: Prevent cross-item branch contamination with a commit-msg hook and a precheck detector.
acceptance_criteria: A commit-msg hook rejects a commit when the branch encodes an item id and the message references a different id (or none); merge/revert commits are skipped.
A precheck gate branch-item re-checks HEAD against the current branch so contamination is caught before merge; wired into precheck fast and ci-cd-gates.
Branches without an item id (develop, release) only warn; the guard never blocks merges/syncs.
Unit tests cover match, mismatch, missing id and merge skip.
in_scope: Guard: commit branch must match the item id in the message
approach: Guard: commit branch must match the item id in the message

assumptions: branch names encode the item id

impact_review.claim: Commit-msg hook can read the message

verification: Objective achieved: Guard: commit branch must match the item id in the message

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing guardrail infrastructure (core/guardrails.py or core/run_guard.py). Add a commit-message/branch-consistency check to the pre-commit hook: parse commit message for item IDs (regex: [A-Z]{2}-[A-Z]+-\d+), extract current branch name, block if an item ID is present in the message but no matching ID appears in the branch name. Configure the new check in config/guardrail-policy.json with an enable/disable flag and optional exemptions list.

analysis.rationale: This is a targeted commit-hygiene check that extends the existing guardrail layer already used by BI-PF-1186. Reuse-first: extend core/guardrails.py and config/guardrail-policy.json with a new branch↔message consistency rule. Low-risk, reversible, config-gated.
assumptions: Pre-commit hook infrastructure and guardrail-policy.json already exist and are active in the target repository
Branch names conventionally contain the item ID (e.g. feature/BI-PF-1472, fix/bi-pf-1472)
Guardrail check is additive and does not require changes to the commit message format
risks: Legitimate squash-merges or cherry-picks may have item IDs in messages that don't match the branch — need exemption path
Multiple item IDs in one commit message — should the guard require ALL or ANY to match the branch
Branch naming conventions may vary across contributors; overly strict check causes friction
